log.msg: Coordinator bug (jsonl streams frozen with Block on) diagnosed and fixed, empirically. Real cause: ext/JSONL/live.js keyed its `streams` Map by the raw jsonl.url a caller passed in, but Server/plugins/SocketServer/Tail.js always echoes a bare url-path with no origin (url_path()) - a caller using import.meta.resolve() (an absolute url, v/3/page.js own board) never matched its own reply, so the live subscribe silently never delivered a frame; the ONLY thing that ever showed a value was live.js own 1.5s client-side timeout falling back to a ONE-TIME fetch(), which ALSO deletes the reader from streams at that moment - so it goes deaf forever until a full reload creates a new subscribe. Proved nothing to do with window.$BLOCKRELOAD: a bare-pathname subscription (says.js own style) streamed every append live with Block on, zero loads, both before and after the fix. Fix: Server/plugins/SocketServer/Tail.js resolve() now reads either an absolute url or a bare path via new URL(url,"http://x/").pathname (defensive, handles any future caller); ext/JSONL/live.js normalizes with the same new URL(url,location.href).pathname at every streams Map touch (stream/drop) and every wire call (subscribe/unsubscribe), so an import.meta.resolve() caller and a bare-pathname caller now key identically and both match the server reply. Proved on the private :8140 server, headless, real socket: pattern A (import.meta.resolve, was broken) now streams every appended line live, Block on and off, 1 total load event across the whole run; pattern B (bare pathname, already correct) unaffected. Separately proved (before this fix, unrelated to it): a jsonl live() stream survives a supervisor-triggered child restart (socket reconnects, live.js resubscribes all active streams on open()) with zero reloads, once the unrelated Directory-on-boot reload-everything broadcast is set aside. v/3/page.js itself needed no edit - the shared fix makes its existing import.meta.resolve() call correct.
log.rule: code#4 (import.meta.resolve is the ordinary way to address a module-relative file) collided with an assumption in Tail.js/live.js that every jsonl url is a bare path

log.msg: CRITICAL bug, self-inflicted, found and fixed: LiveReload.js poll_hold() called this.socket_server.sockets synchronously inside initialize() - but LiveReload.setup() runs from DevSocket static new event, which Events.js fires BEFORE the emitting SocketServer instance reaches its OWN initialize() (where sockets=[] is set), so sockets was undefined at that exact moment. Harmless when no hold is on disk at boot (the broadcast branch is skipped), but a live hold at boot threw TypeError: is not iterable and crashed the child - this took the mastermind real supervised :8123 down while I was mid-task (coordinator alert), and would have crashed the owners own server at their next restart too. Also exposed a second, separate bug in server.js own supervisor: restart() attaches old.once("exit",...) to a child that may already be dead by the time it attaches, which can wedge restarting=true forever and stop ALL future restarts silently - hit this on my OWN private :8140 instance (had to kill the supervisor by its real PID and boot fresh; did not touch server.js, out of fence, flagged for the owner instead). Fix: initialize() now defers the first poll_hold() and the 500ms interval until this.socket_server.server emits listening (Server.js, after http.listen() callback - by which point SocketServer.initialize() has long since set sockets), plus a defensive ?? [] on the broadcast loop itself. Proved on the private server: three fresh boots (no hold / a live hold already on disk / an expired-but-not-yet-pruned hold) each reached exactly one "Server listening" line and answered curl 200, zero TypeErrors in any of the three logs. Confirmed http://localhost:8123/ back to 200 and posted one line to the owners log via the assistant skills say.mjs, per the coordinators instruction. Lesson written into the minion skill paragraph below: node --check only proves a file parses, never that initialize() runs without throwing - boot any edited Server/ file on a private port and curl it before moving on, every time.
log.rule: code#2 (Events.js emits "new" before instantiate()/initialize() - a plugin built from that hook cannot assume its host has finished its own initialize() yet)

log.msg: Second real bug found by my own final visual check, fixed: a tab that CONNECTS after a hold is already active never received a hold rpc at all, because poll_hold only broadcast on a SIGNATURE CHANGE, global across all sockets - a late-joining tab (the owner opening a fresh tab while an agent is mid-batch) saw no readout even though held. Fixed: LiveReload now tracks which sockets have ever been sent a frame (a WeakSet) and syncs any new one on its very next poll regardless of whether the signature moved. Proved: a tab opened AFTER taking a hold (not before) now reads held by final-check, 82s within one poll tick; booted clean on the private server first (curl 200, zero TypeErrors) before trusting it, per the new habit.
log.rule: code#2 and the new minion lesson - boot and curl every Server/ edit before trusting it

assign.outcome:
**The reload hold landed and is proven.** One command before a batch of writes — `node Server/hold.mjs on "<who> — <what>"` — then the writes, then `node Server/hold.mjs off "<who>"`: every server watching this repo (owner's, mastermind's, any private one) queues every change and sends nothing until the last hold releases, then ONE reload for the whole batch. `.jsonl` streams (chat, the AI board) are a separate channel and keep flowing throughout. Proven on a private `:8140` server with real `load`-event counts: 3 files held 10s → 0 reloads, released → exactly 1; two holders (first release does nothing, second flushes); a 5-second test expiry flushes itself and logs it; a supervisor restart mid-hold stays held. Shown in the dev bar beside Block, and on a live demo page: [Reload hold](/framework/ai/2026-09-19/reload-hold/).

**Two real crashes found and fixed, not gone looking for.** (1) The owner's own report — chat/board streams looked frozen unless Block was unchecked — had nothing to do with Block: `ext/JSONL/live.js` keyed its stream registry by whatever url a caller passed, and `import.meta.resolve()` (an ordinary way to build one) never matched the server's reply, so that reader went silently deaf after one fallback fetch. Fixed in `live.js` and `Tail.js`; proven live with Block ON. (2) My own hold code crashed the child at boot whenever a hold was already on disk, and took the mastermind's real `:8123` down for about four minutes while this task was running. Fixed (the first poll now waits for the server's own "listening" event), `:8123` confirmed back to 200, three clean private-server boots proven (no hold / a live hold / an expired hold). A third gap — a tab that connects AFTER a hold is already on never saw the readout — was caught by my own check and fixed the same way.

**Hot reload, briefly.** CSS already hot-swaps with zero reloads (Socket.js's existing `restyle()`) — confirmed, nothing new to ship. A page CAN re-import its own module and live-swap into the Router with no navigation (a real working button on the demo page) — but it duplicates the module's own state and its stylesheet `<link>` every time, nothing cleaning up either copy, so it stays an experiment, never a default. A shared module (`core/View`) still needs a full reload: every page on screen holds its own reference to it.

**Propose for CLAUDE.md** (not edited — for the mastermind to land): *"Before a batch of writes that touch a file the live site loads: `node Server/hold.mjs on "<you> — <what>"`, write the batch, `node Server/hold.mjs off "<you>"` — one reload instead of one per file. It holds every server watching this repo, not just yours, and expires on its own after 5 minutes."*

**Reaches the owner now vs. at their next restart:** the client files (`live.js`, `Socket.js`, the dev-bar readout) serve fresh from disk on their very next page load. The hold mechanism and both crash fixes live under `Server/` and only reach their server at its next restart.

**Left:** page re-import stays a demo, not a feature — the study's own verdict. `server.js`'s supervisor has a second, separate bug (`restart()` can wedge itself and silently stop restarting forever if a child is already dead when `.once("exit")` attaches) — hit once on my own private server, outside my fence, flagged here for the owner.
